code_findings.finding: The root cause is alert emission for a failed Attempt while its Run still has running status and retry eligibility. The baseline shows two persisted alert ids for the same Run across two Attempts, rather than transport duplication or separate Runs.

The current service is byte-for-byte identical to the initial service after deleting only self._emit_failure_alert(run_id) from the retry branch. This removes the lifecycle error without storage deduplication, schema changes, or Job-wide suppression.

The only remaining service emission follows set_run_status(run_id, failed). The success branch returns before emission. The existing non-running guard remains before add_attempt. Attempt insertion, max_attempts comparison, retry response and stable Run identity are unchanged.

Distinct failed Runs of the same Job retain one alert each. New public tests exercise distinct manual and scheduled Runs across retry limits 1, 2 and 3 and compare actual alert payloads and Run ids. No deduplication key was introduced.

Eventual success produces no failure alerts and is paired with a positive failed-Run control. Retry state and attempt numbers/outcomes are asserted through API responses and the existing Store fixture interface. The API tests execute actual WSGI logic and contain substantive positive assertions.

The 115-line test addition is proportional to the lifecycle cases. Assertions cover public state, alert kind/message/identity and deterministic attempt progression, rather than private call counts or source structure. Original tests are unchanged.

The exact test-only commit contains only the new regression file.

Preserved focused output reports 3 test methods OK. Full public output reports all 8 methods OK. The lead independently reran the original API script and observed zero alerts during retry and one terminal alert with attempts [1, 2]. Exit codes in commands.jsonl agree with these outputs.

All 13 existing decision-row evidence pointers resolve. Runtime, source, commit, design and verification evidence substantiate the selected deletion. Two design sketches distinguish lifecycle-policy deletion from storage deduplication, which would retain the premature alert. Four throughput items were recorded before implementation delegation.
